text: Franco Bassanini, born on 9 May 1940, is an Italian lawyer, politician, minister, and undersecretary of state. He was born in Milan and served as a deputy from 1979 to 1996 and as a senator from 1996 to 2006. From 1996 to 2001, he held the position of minister of public administration and regional affairs in the cabinets of Romano Prodi, Massimo D'Alema, and Giuliano Amato. Bassanini was president of Astrid, a think-tank focused on institutional and administrative reform. As a member of the administrative council of the ENA, he was appointed by Nicolas Sarkozy in 2007 to join the Commission pour la libération de la croissance française, chaired by Jacques Attali, with the aim of reforming France's administration. A member of the Italy-USA Foundation, he taught constitutional law at the First University of Rome and served as chairman of Cassa Depositi e Prestiti. He is also a member of the advisory board of the Official and Financial Institutions Forum (OMFIF), where he regularly participates in discussions on the financial and monetary system.
